title: Apple Stock Is Tumbling After It Warned of Weak iPhone Sales in China
text:

https://www.barrons.com/articles/apple-sharply-lowers-its-guidance-51546465862 Apple Stock Is Tumbling After It Warned of Weak iPhone Sales in China By Updated Jan. 3, 2019 9:04 a.m. ET Order Reprints Apple CEO Tim Cook. Photograph by Timothy A. Clary/AFP/Getty Images Text size
Apple (AAPL) on Wednesday lowered its financial guidance for its December quarter.
“We expected economic weakness in some emerging markets. This turned out to have a significantly greater impact than we had projected,” CEO Tim Cook said in a news release. “While we anticipated some challenges in key emerging markets, we did not foresee the magnitude of the economic deceleration, particularly in Greater China.”
Apple stock dropped 7.5% in after-hours trading on Wednesday, and was 8.8% in pre-market trading on Thursday, to $144 a share. That drop outpaced a 1.6% drop in futures for the Nasdaq 100 index. ﻿ Stock in Apple suppliers, which had already been facing headwinds amid reports the company had cut iPhone orders, took another hit Thursday in Asia trading .
Apple said it now expects sales of approximately $84 billion for the December quarter versus the Wall Street consensus of $91.3 billion, according to FactSet.
On Nov. 1, 2018, Apple gave sales outlook range of $89 billion and $93 billion for the December quarter.
Cook blamed China as the key driver for the lowered sales guidance. China generated 18% of the company’s sales in its September quarter.
“In fact, most of our revenue shortfall to our guidance, and over 100 percent of our year-over-year worldwide revenue decline, occurred in Greater China across iPhone, Mac and iPad,” he added.
The company’s shares had already declined nearly 30% since the end of October as concerns had mounted about weak demand for the iPhone models released last fall, amid a number of smartphone supplier warnings.
The announcement did have a silver lining.
Cook said Apple’s cash generation remains robust and added the company will end December with a net cash position of $130 billion. He restated Apple’s goal to be “net-cash neutral” over time, basically hinting at larger share buybacks or dividends.
